title: Audit fingerprint specification and operator delegation UX notes
content:
Summary:

This draft defines a compact, privacy-minimizing "audit fingerprint" that captures the minimal cryptographic evidence needed to prove a VPC/network/operator change occurred and was approved, without shipping full packet logs or sensitive configs to Redwood. The goal is a practical tradeoff: high forensic value for investigators + tiny storage/egress footprint + strong customer control.

Context / why this exists (notes):
- Customers (regulated, finance, healthcare) want tamper-evident proof of infrastructure/approval events but are often unwilling to export raw logs.
- Existing proposals in the folder are heavy (full evidence bundles) or require always-on telemetry. We need a middle ground: small per-change artifacts that can be expanded-on-demand.
- This ties to the Private product onboarding flow and operator delegation story: operators (customer-side) should be able to assert short-term approvals and optionally attach deeper evidence if an audit is triggered.

Core concept: Audit Fingerprint (AF)
- What it is: a short, deterministic, cryptographic summary of a change event (JSON) + signatures. The AF is stored by Redwood (immutable) and optionally escrowed by the customer.
- Size target: <= 1.5KB per change (compressed)
- Properties: deterministic, tamper-evident, privacy-minimizing, verifiable offline.

Candidate AF JSON schema (human-readable variant):
- af_version: "1.0"
- change_id: uuid v4 (deterministic from event fields)
- ts_utc: ISO8601 timestamp
- actor: {actor_type, actor_id_hash}  // actor_id hashed (sha256) to avoid PII in Redwood store
- scope_hash: sha256(base64-encoded minimal scope descriptor)  // e.g. subnet tags, allowed ports matrix in canonical order
- approval_policy: short enum (AUTO, OPERATOR, LEGAL_ESCALATE)
- approval_assertion: {assertion_type, assertion_signature_b64} // assertion_signature uses customer KMS key or Redwood delegated signer
- ephemeral_proof_refs: [compact reference ids] // pointers to deeper artifacts customer retains or escrowed blob ids
- runtime_hash: sha256(binary of runtime manifest snapshot) // small manifest of model image + config fingerprint
- evidence_flags: CSV (captures what deeper artifacts exist off-store: "syslog_grep,pcap_digest,console_snapshot")
- fingerprint: base64url(sha256(serialized-above-blocks))  // final atomic digest stored and indexed

Notes about fields and privacy-preserving choices:
- actor_id is hashed so Redwood can't trivially map to human names. Customers can provide a mapping if they choose.
- scope descriptor must be canonicalized (sorted keys, normalized names) to ensure same change yields same change_id when appropriate.
- evidence_refs are NOT raw data. They are stable identifiers (customer-side) that can be exchanged during an audit request with proof-of-possession.

Assertions and signatures model:
- Two modes: (A) Customer-signed: customer signs the AF with their KMS-managed key (recommended). (B) Redwood-attested: Redwood signs with our delegated acceptance key after verifying approval gate conditions.
- We need KMS integrations: Cloud KMS / HSM options and a fallback for customers that cannot use KMS (paper-assertion workflow).

Approval gates UX (operator flow):
- Lightweight flow (low-risk changes): operator triggers change -> client computes AF locally -> operator approves inside customer console -> signature stored locally + AF copy sent to Redwood store (fingerprint only).
- Escalated flow (sensitive changes): operator marks for escalation -> legal/operator-review -> deeper evidence snapshot requested from customer (optional upload) -> AF updated with evidence_refs and Redwood attestation if accepted.

Console mockups / UX notes (rough):
- Onboarding modal: "Configure compact audit fingerprints" -> toggles: store fingerprints at Redwood (yes/no), escrow to S3 (yes/no), enable on-demand evidence upload (yes/no).
- Change timeline UI: each row shows timestamp, approval_policy, fingerprint, short status (OK / ESCALATED / UNDER-AUDIT). Clicking opens a panel with: canonical scope summary (not sensitive), proof-trace (who signed), and: "Request full evidence" button (customer consent required).
- Operator delegation panel: allow manager to create time-boxed delegate tokens (e.g., 4h, scope-limited) which the operator uses to sign approvals. Tokens are recorded as actor_type=delegate and hashed id stored in AF.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- AF schema v1 implemented server-side; Redwood can store and immutably index fingerprint + metadata in append-only ledger.
- Customer CLI/agent can emit AF for the three test change types (subnet add, route change, egress ACL update).
- Customer KMS signing integration demonstrated with two cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS).
- Console surfaces change timeline and provides "Request full evidence" flow that triggers an audit request email to customer operators and creates a ticket in JIRA-PD-3321.
- Storage cost: baseline < 2KB per event stored; support retention policies (30/90/365d).

Metrics to validate:
- Fingerprint volume per customer per day (target < 500/day for most SMBs).
- % of fingerprints with evidence_refs (target < 10% in normal ops; higher for pilots).
- Time-to-first-signature (operator latency) and audit-request acceptance rate.
- Storage bytes saved vs full evidence baseline (goal: >60% reduction).

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal): prototype AF generator + indexer; manual signing keys; basic console view (internal only).
- Phase 1 (pilot): 2 pilot customers in fintech; integrate AWS KMS; enable escrow to S3 for pilot.
- Phase 2 (GA): add GCP KMS, RBAC for operators, retention UI, programmatic audit request API.
- Phase 3: toolbox: automated replay harness (when full evidence is provided), query federation to customer-supplied evidence stores.

Dependencies and open infra work:
- Append-only index/ledger: storage and query patterns; how we immutably store fingerprint + minimal metadata (also tie to existing attestation ledger designs in repo).
- KMS integrations (AWS/GCP/Azure), plus HSM for on-prem customers.
- Customer-side small agent / CLI that canonicalizes changes and emits AFs. This will live in solutions-engineering repo and needs SDKs.
- Console/UX work for timeline, delegation, and audit request flows (product + devexp).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customers treat AF as a replacement for full evidence and then mid-audit we need full logs. Mitigation: clear UX and SLA that AF is a pointer + optional light evidence; require opt-in for full evidence escrow.
- Risk: Hash collisions / canonicalization mistakes create mismatch. Mitigation: provide canonicalization library with tests and include version in AF.
- Risk: Legal/regulatory teams won't accept hashed actor ids. Mitigation: allow customer-side mapping export for audits under NDAs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the exact canonical scope descriptor format? (TODO: create spec + examples for subnet/route/acl).
- How does long-term evidence escrow work for customers that require >7 years retention? (legal).
- Delegation tokens: JWT vs short-lived KMS-signed blobs? (security team to decide).
- UX: should AFs be searchable by customer-supplied labels (we currently only store fingerprint + small metadata)?

Next steps (immediate):
- Engineering spike for AF canonicalization library (owner: Liam) — 2 week spike.
- Console prototype for timeline and "Request full evidence" (owner: Hannah) — mockups by next sprint.
- Reach out to two pilot customers for interest in compact-proof pilot (owner: Priya).

Notes to self: rough example AF for a subnet change (illustrative, redacted):
- change_id: 8a3c...
- ts_utc: 2024-09-12T18:22:11Z
- actor: {"operator","sha256:3f2a..."}
- scope_hash: sha256:9b2f...  (represents subnet-id + cidr + tag-set)
- approval_policy: OPERATOR
- evidence_flags: "syslog_grep"
- fingerprint: base64url:XA9z...

If this direction looks promising I will:
1) draft a minimal RFC for canonical scope formats + test vectors,
2) kick off the engineering spike and attach to JIRA-PD-3321,
3) prepare one-pager for pilot customers describing benefits & privacy model.

-- end of draft --
